subject: Evidence buckets, BYO exception & SSO handshake — Cardinal pilot
messages:
From: Alice Martin <alice@cardinalhealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@cardinalhealth.com
Date: Sun, 12 Dec 2026 09:07:00 -0500
Subject: Pilot request — evidence categories + temporary BYO exception

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. We have three immediate asks from our security and procurement teams to get the pilot moving: 1) a clear mapping of what audit evidence Redwood can provide (audit logs, object-level retention, export windows), 2) a proposed temporary BYO (customer KMS) exception for the pilot (60 days) and what controls accompany that, and 3) confirmation of SSO handshake timing for provisioning (Okta).

I attached a quick spreadsheet with the evidence items our auditors expect (cardinal-evidence-list.csv). Can you confirm which items are covered out-of-the-box vs. require manual evidence pulls or engineering support? Procurement also needs a short summary PDF for legal on the proposed exception.

Goal: have a mutual action plan by EOD Wednesday.

Appreciate it —
Alice Martin
Sr. InfoSec Program Manager
Cardinal Health

Attachments: cardinal-evidence-list.csv
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Alice Martin <alice@cardinalhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Dec 2026 10:12:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Pilot request — evidence categories + temporary BYO exception

Alice — thanks, and great list. Looping in security product (Ben), ops/orchestration (Priyom) and compliance lead (Marissa) to triage. A few immediate clarifications from our side:

- Scope: pilot will run against the sandbox tenant you shared, retention windows will be per-tenant but our standard export endpoints cover auditlog, auth events, and request/response metadata. Object-level deletion proofs are a manual pull today.
- BYO exception: we can support a 60-day temporary BYOK arrangement if Cardinal provides a short-lived key and agrees to escrow and delete controls (we'll draft language). This will require a scoped exception ticket and a short implementation run (1 week).
- SSO: Okta handshake typically completes in 2 business days once we get the SAML metadata. We can do a parallel provisioning test with one admin user.

Action items:
1) Ben: confirm which evidence items are automated vs manual from product side (audit, auth, request/response, keystore change logs).
2) Priyom: estimate ops work for temporary BYOK route (+ rollback).
3) Marissa: draft two-paragraph summary for procurement that covers controls and monitoring.

We’ll aim for a consolidated reply to Cardinal by EOD Wednesday.

—Irene
Irene Choi
Manager, Security & Compliance (Redwood)

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Dec 2026 08:42:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Pilot request — evidence categories + temporary BYO exception

Quick notes from product/security:

- Automated: system-level audit logs (admin actions), auth events (SSO success/fail), API request/response headers (meta tokens, timestamps), model variant and invocation records. These are exportable via our audit-export API on a daily cadence.
- Semi-automated/manual: per-object deletion receipts and immutable object snapshots are not currently exported automatically; we can run a one-off evidence pack and attach hashes for the pilot (we should record the process).
- Keystore logs: encryption key rotation events are emitted but currently held in internal telemetry — Ops will need a small plumbing change to expose a curated, tamper-evident rotation history to customers (I estimate 3–4 dev days).

Temporary BYOK plan (high level):
- Scope the exception: pilot-only, single tenant, 60-day TTL on imported key, keys provided via secure upload to our escrow service.
- Controls: RBAC for key usage, signed audit of every call that used the BYO key, automated deletion of the key after TTL.
- Risks: longer retention of customer-provided keys impedes rotation; we will require a signed acceptance from the customer acknowledging risk.

I’ll draft the technical appendix for Marissa’s procurement note. Priyom: if ops can estimate the plumbing change for the keystore rotation exposure, add that to the delivery plan.

Ben
Head of Security Product

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Dec 2026 09:15:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Pilot request — evidence categories + temporary BYO exception

Ops estimate and constraints:

- Temporary BYOK flow: approx 5 engineering-days + 2 QA-days for the scoped path (secure upload endpoint, short-term escrow store, TTL enforcement, and deletion validation). Can cut to ~3 eng days if we re-use the existing one-off escrow tooling (requires a config flag and a manual runbook).
- Keystore rotation events exposure: small API change + retention policy docs — about 3 eng days. We should not expose raw telemetry; ops will curate a signed event stream.
- SSO provisioning: once we get SAML metadata from Cardinal we can create the tenant and do a smoke test same-day; Okta provisioning requires their admin to approve the SAML cert exchange.

Proposed timeline (assuming Cardinal signs off by Wednesday EOD):
- Thu Dec 16: draft procurement summary and technical appendix (Marissa + Ben)
- Mon Dec 20: ops prepare escrow config and start validation
- Tue Dec 21 – Fri Dec 24: engineering work window for keystore-exposure + BYOK path (parallelizable)

I’m attaching a sample acceptance script for the deletion validation and proposed rollout steps.

Attachments: redwood-temp-byo-sla-v1.pdf

—Priyom
Principal Engineer, Orchestration
From: Alice Martin <alice@cardinalhealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@cardinalhealth.com, AuditHub Support <support@audithub.io>
Date: Wed, 15 Dec 2026 16:20:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Pilot request — evidence categories + temporary BYO exception

Team — thanks for the quick triage and the clear plan. Cardinal approves moving forward with the 60-day temporary BYOK pilot under the controls you outlined. Two asks before you start: 1) a one-page procurement summary for our legal that includes the risk acknowledgment language, and 2) a target window for the SSO handshake (we need identified admins on our side).

We’ll upload the SAML metadata to the shared Drive link you provided and procurement will review the PDF. Targeting sign-off today so engineering can start Monday.

Alice
Sr. InfoSec Program Manager
Cardinal Health
